title: Asymmetric capacity fanout loop analysis and action items
creator: Riley Chen
description: Incident summary: On 2026-02-26 ~09:12 UTC we observed a sustained cross-region reroute loop that increased p95 latency and caused a spike in fallbacks to lower-quality model variants. Traffic for a subset of customers was repeatedly bounced between us-west-2 and eu-west-1 for ~23 minutes, causing token amplification and degraded availability for embargoed Dedicated pools. This ticket consolidates the analysis, short-term mitigations, and longer-term action items.
postmortem_summary: What happened: A recent policy rollout introduced asymmetric capacity weights for a new variant group while the policy cache TTL and route-header propagation resulted in stale precedence for 2 minutes. The combination caused the smart-router to treat capacity-constrained region as eligible and then immediately fan out to the other region where a transient throttling event triggered another reroute back, creating a loop. The loop escalated because KV prefix cache and telemetry lacked a fast feedback signal causing fallbacks to cascade to quantized variants. Impact: increased latency, higher token cost, and several Dedicated customers hit error budgets. Duration: ~23 minutes. Detection: automated SLO alerting and on-call noticing cache-thrashing metrics.
root_cause: 1) Policy rollout allowed a new weighted variant configuration without a preflight consistency check. 2) Policy cache TTL (120s) was longer than the policy-staging window; stale policy state persisted across route evaluations. 3) Router's fanout logic did not have a symmetry guard—requests could be retried in a way that created circular handoffs. 4) Telemetry did not expose per-variant cross-region fanout counters at alerting granularity.
immediate_mitigation: Rolled back the weighted-variant config, temporarily reduced policy cache TTL to 15s, and enabled a routing circuit-breaker that blocks symmetric cross-region fanout if the same request UUID is observed twice within 10s. These changes were deployed within 12 minutes of detection and stabilized traffic.
action_items: (A1) Router: add asymmetric-fanout detector & enforce single-pass routing per request UUID (owner: Aisha Khan) — due 2026-03-18
(A2) Policy rollout: implement preflight consistency check that simulates variant-selection scoring and rejects configs that create >= 2x fanout risk (owner: Marcus Liao) — due 2026-04-01
(A3) Cache: reduce default policy TTL and add an atomic policy invalidation API used during rollouts (owner: Priya Patel) — due 2026-03-24
(A4) Telemetry: add per-variant cross-region fanout counters and high-cardinality histograms; create an SLO alert (owner: Diego Morales) — due 2026-03-17
(A5) Runbook: update routing incident playbook with steps to identify and kill fanout loops, and include a checklist for rollback vs TTL tuning (owner: Jordan Blake) — due 2026-03-12
(A6) Tests: add integration test in staging that runs synthetic asymmetric-capacity scenarios and asserts no persistent reroute loops (owner: Sangeeta Rao) — due 2026-03-31
(A7) Observability: backfill 30d of router request UUIDs linked to variant decisions to help root-cause audits (owner: Analytics team) — due 2026-04-07
progress_updates: 2026-02-26 09:40 UTC — Emergency rollback of weighted-variant config succeeded; p95 latency returned to baseline within 5 minutes (update by Riley Chen)
2026-02-26 10:05 UTC — Short-term TTL reduction and circuit-breaker deployed (update by Aisha Khan)
2026-03-02 — Initial draft of fanout detector merged to staging; still requires load testing (update by Aisha Khan)
2026-03-07 — Telemetry schema PR open: added fanout counters and a dashboard; awaiting infra review (update by Diego Morales)
2026-03-09 — Runbook patch landed; incident playbook section for fanout loops added (update by Jordan Blake)
acceptance_criteria: Routing no longer allows sustained symmetric cross-region fanout in synthetic tests
Policy rollout preflight rejects configurations with simulated >1.5x fanout risk
SLO alert fires within 1 minute of cross-region fanout rate breaching threshold
Runbook contains clear step-by-step mitigation and confirmed on-call training

SRE (2026-03-08): Circuit-breaker logic should be parameterized by customer tier; Dedicated customers get a more aggressive safety threshold.
